claims.text: The bulk magnetocaloric response of FeMnNiGeSi is underlain by a magnetostructural transformation.
Greater interfacial constraint and reduced domain size suppress the magnetostructural transformation in low-dimensional FeMnNiGeSi films.
Nanoscale size constraints diminish the magnetocaloric temperature or entropy change relative to bulk-like material.
Greater interfacial constraint and reduced domain size enhance magnetic hysteresis.
Increasing FeMnNiGeSi film thickness from 20 nm toward 200 nm can partially restore its magnetocaloric response.
The controlled intervention is to vary film thickness through 20, 50, 100, and 200 nm while holding composition and deposition conditions fixed.
Finite-size and interfacial constraints affect the magnetostructural transformation.
Finite-size and interfacial constraints affect domain-wall mobility.
Increasing film thickness promotes strain relaxation.
Increasing film thickness reduces the interface-to-volume ratio.
Strain relaxation and a reduced interface-to-volume ratio enhance cooperative magnetic transitions.
Enhanced cooperative magnetic transitions increase the magnetocaloric effect.
Enhanced cooperative magnetic transitions reduce hysteresis.
Thicker films will exhibit larger isothermal entropy changes than the 20 nm as-deposited baseline.
Thicker films will exhibit smaller hysteresis losses than the 20 nm as-deposited baseline.
The proposed operating range is 20–200 nm thickness, fields no greater than 2 T, and temperatures of approximately 80–350 K.
Residual stress or thickness-dependent composition shifts may alter the magnetocaloric trend.
No detectable dependence of magnetocaloric response or hysteresis on thickness would falsify the proposed finite-size and interfacial-constraint mechanism.
